# Traefik Research Notes

## What is Traefik?

Traefik is a cloud-native reverse proxy and ingress controller for Kubernetes. It automatically discovers services via Kubernetes providers (Ingress, CRD, Gateway API) and routes HTTP/TCP/UDP traffic to them. It is widely used as a Kubernetes Ingress controller and as a general-purpose edge router.

- GitHub: https://github.com/traefik/traefik
- Docs: https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/
- CNCF incubating project

## Installation

- **Method**: Helm chart (`traefik/traefik`)
- **Chart repo**: https://traefik.github.io/charts
- **Latest version tested**: Chart 40.0.0 / App v3.7.0
- **Namespace**: `traefik`
- **CRDs**: Installed automatically by the chart (IngressRoute, Middleware, TLSOption, etc.)

## Telemetry Capabilities

### Traces
- **Protocol**: OTLP (gRPC or HTTP) — native, first-class support
- **SDK**: opentelemetry-go v1.43.0 (embedded in Traefik binary)
- **Scope**: `github.com/traefik/traefik` (no version in scope)
- **Span types observed**:
  - `GET` — entry-point server spans (kind=SERVER, uses OTel semantic conventions: `http.request.method`, `url.path`, `url.scheme`, `network.protocol.version`, `http.response.status_code`)
  - `ReverseProxy` — upstream forwarding spans (kind=CLIENT)
  - Internal spans when `tracing.addInternals: true` is set
- **Context propagation**: W3C Trace Context (traceparent) — confirmed working. When a request carries a `traceparent` header, Traefik joins the existing trace (same `traceId` observed in spans).
- **Sample rate**: Configurable (default 1.0)
- **Configuration**: `tracing.otlp.grpc.enabled: true` in Helm values

### Metrics
Traefik supports **two concurrent metrics export paths**:

#### OTLP Metrics (push)
- **Protocol**: OTLP gRPC (or HTTP)
- **SDK**: opentelemetry-go (same as tracing)
- **Scope**: `github.com/traefik/traefik`
- **Key metrics** (Traefik-native, via OTLP):
  - `traefik_entrypoint_requests_total` — request count by entrypoint, method, protocol, status
  - `traefik_entrypoint_request_duration_seconds` — latency histogram
  - `traefik_entrypoint_requests_bytes_total` / `traefik_entrypoint_responses_bytes_total`
  - `traefik_router_requests_total` / `traefik_router_request_duration_seconds`
  - `traefik_router_requests_bytes_total` / `traefik_router_responses_bytes_total`
  - `traefik_service_requests_total` / `traefik_service_request_duration_seconds`
  - `traefik_service_requests_bytes_total` / `traefik_service_responses_bytes_total`
  - `traefik_open_connections`
  - `traefik_config_reloads_total` / `traefik_config_last_reload_success`
  - `http.server.request.duration` (OTel semantic convention histogram)
  - `http.client.request.duration` (OTel semantic convention histogram)
- **Configuration**: `metrics.otlp.grpc.enabled: true`

#### Prometheus (pull/scrape)
- **Endpoint**: `:9100/metrics` (dedicated metrics entrypoint)
- **Metrics**: Same set of `traefik_*` metrics plus Go runtime metrics (`go_*`, `process_*`)
- **Service**: `traefik-metrics` ClusterIP service on port 9100
- **Configuration**: `metrics.prometheus.service.enabled: true`

### Logs
- **Protocol**: OTLP gRPC (experimental feature, requires `experimental.otlpLogs: true`)
- **Two log streams**:
  1. **General logs** (`log.otlp`): Traefik operational logs (startup, config changes, errors)
  2. **Access logs** (`accesslog.otlp`): Per-request access logs with rich fields
- **Access log fields** (observed in log body as JSON string + structured attributes):
  - `RequestMethod`, `RequestPath`, `RequestHost`, `RequestProtocol`
  - `DownstreamStatus`, `DownstreamContentSize`
  - `Duration`, `OriginDuration`, `Overhead`
  - `RouterName`, `ServiceName`, `ServiceAddr`
  - `TraceId`, `SpanId` (trace correlation in access logs)
  - `KubernetesIngressName`, `KubernetesIngressNamespace`, `KubernetesServiceName`
  - `entryPointName`
- **Severity**: Access logs use `info` severity; general logs use appropriate levels
- **Scope**: `traefik`
- **Note**: The log body is a JSON string (not a structured map). Fields are also promoted to log record attributes. This is a known Traefik behavior — it serializes the access log struct to JSON and sends it as the body string, while also populating attributes.

## Context Propagation

- **Format**: W3C Trace Context (`traceparent` header)
- **Behavior**: Confirmed — when a request carries a `traceparent` header, Traefik participates in the same trace (same `traceId` in Traefik spans and downstream backend spans)
- **Propagation to upstream**: Traefik injects `traceparent` into forwarded requests, so the backend receives the same trace context

## Resource Attributes (project-native, pre-collector enrichment)

Traefik emits a rich set of resource attributes natively via the OTel SDK:
- `service.name: traefik`
- `service.version: 3.7.0`
- `telemetry.sdk.name: opentelemetry`
- `telemetry.sdk.language: go`
- `telemetry.sdk.version: 1.43.0`
- `host.name: <pod-name>` (from Go runtime)
- `os.type: linux`
- `os.description: Alpine Linux ...`
- `process.pid`, `process.executable.name`, `process.executable.path`, `process.owner`
- `process.runtime.name: go`, `process.runtime.version`, `process.runtime.description`
- `process.command_args` (full CLI args array — very verbose, includes all config flags)

**Collector-added** (via k8sattributes processor):
- `k8s.namespace.name`, `k8s.pod.name`, `k8s.pod.uid`, `k8s.pod.start_time`
- `k8s.deployment.name`, `k8s.replicaset.name`, `k8s.node.name`, `k8s.container.name`
- Pod labels and annotations

## Special Setup Notes

- **CRDs**: Traefik installs its own CRDs (IngressRoute, Middleware, etc.) automatically
- **RBAC**: Helm chart creates ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding for Kubernetes API access
- **OTLP Logs are experimental**: Requires `experimental.otlpLogs: true` in Helm values (Traefik v3 feature)
- **Service type**: Default is LoadBalancer; must override to ClusterIP for kind clusters (`service.spec.type: ClusterIP`)
- **Metrics service**: A separate `traefik-metrics` ClusterIP service is created when `metrics.prometheus.service.enabled: true`
- **`addInternals`**: Setting `tracing.addInternals: true` and `metrics.addInternals: true` adds telemetry for Traefik's own internal routing (ping, dashboard, etc.)

## Actual Observations vs Documentation

- Documentation says OTLP logs are experimental; confirmed working in v3.7.0 with `experimental.otlpLogs: true`
- Access log OTLP export sends log body as a JSON string (not structured), but also populates log record attributes — slightly inconsistent but functional
- `process.command_args` in resource attributes is extremely verbose (contains all CLI flags), which is unusual for a resource attribute
- Prometheus scrape and OTLP metrics push run concurrently without conflict — both export the same `traefik_*` metrics
- The `traefik_*` metric names in OTLP use the same names as Prometheus (not translated to OTel conventions), except for the two OTel semantic convention histograms (`http.server.request.duration`, `http.client.request.duration`)
